rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all six peaks and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The retention window will guide subsequent gradient trimming and selectivity tests.

Injection 1 already achieved the maximum possible CRF of 1.000. Shorten the gradient by one step to test whether full resolution can be maintained in less time, retaining injection 1 as the proven optimum-score method.

The 8-minute gradient preserves maximum CRF with minimum resolution 3.24, leaving substantial margin. Shorten by another grid step while holding temperature and solvent endpoints fixed to seek a faster fully resolved method.
Shorten the gradient another step to reduce analysis time while preserving the already maximal CRF. The observed resolution trend suggests the critical pair may remain above 1.5 at four minutes.

The four-minute gradient retains maximum CRF, but its critical pair has little resolution margin for further steepening. Raise temperature to test whether faster elution and favorable selectivity can preserve full resolution.

Heating worsened the critical pair, so test the lowest temperature to improve its selectivity while shortening the gradient to two minutes. The high final organic fraction ensures a strong elution hold; injection 4 remains the fastest proven maximum-score method.

Narrowing the gradient lowers its slope enough to potentially bring the critical pair above R = 1.5 while retaining the two-minute ramp. The last peak will elute during the final hold, so this run also tests whether 0.75 organic provides sufficiently rapid elution.

Shift both solvent endpoints upward while preserving the slope that resolved every pair in injection 7. The stronger final hold should accelerate the last peak; this tests whether the early pair retains sufficient resolution at the higher starting organic fraction.

Shift the gradient window upward another step at the same slope and temperature, since the previous shift preserved the critical resolution of 1.59. A stronger final hold should shorten late elution further while testing the early pair’s tolerance to increased starting organic.

Continue shifting the window upward at unchanged slope to accelerate the last peak while preserving the selectivity seen in injections 7–9. Monitor the first pair closely as its elution approaches the early, weakly retained region.

Shift both endpoints upward once more at the proven slope, reaching the strongest permitted final solvent. This should shorten late elution while testing whether the first pair remains fully resolved as its retention decreases.

Raise only the starting organic fraction to shorten retention further while making the gradient slightly shallower. This may improve gradient selectivity, but the first pair must be checked for compression near the unretained region.

Test a five-degree temperature increase to shorten late retention while using the critical pair’s improved resolution margin of 1.77. Keep the solvent window fixed because the first peak is already close to the weakly retained region.

Test whether a narrower gradient can shorten late elution without collapsing the early pair, returning to 25 C for its better selectivity. This probes the upper starting-organic boundary; injection 13 remains the fastest proven fully resolved method.

Return to the starting fraction that avoids early-pair collapse and test one temperature step above the fastest fully resolved method. This brackets the thermal resolution limit; the observed trend suggests the critical pair may fall slightly below 1.5.

Reduce the final organic fraction one step to test whether a shallower gradient restores the critical pair’s resolution at 35 C. This trades some late-peak hold time for separation; injection 13 remains the fastest proven maximum-score method.

Shift injection 16’s window downward at unchanged slope to retain the early pair beyond the gradient-delay region, where slope can improve its separation. This tests whether full resolution can be recovered at 35 C, with a modest increase in late-peak hold time.

Return to 30 C and shift the fastest fully resolved method’s window downward at unchanged slope. This tests a maximum-score alternative with the first pair farther from the unretained region, accepting slightly slower late elution.

Lower temperature one step from injection 18 to improve the critical pair’s narrow resolution margin while keeping early peaks away from the unretained region. This seeks a more robust maximum-score alternative; injection 13 remains the fastest proven fully resolved method.

Test a one-step reduction in final organic relative to injection 13 to assess whether its critical-pair margin improves while retaining rapid elution. The maximum CRF is already secured, and injection 13 remains the fastest proven fully resolved method.

Lower temperature one step from injection 20 to increase the critical-pair resolution margin while keeping the two-minute gradient. This refines the nearby maximum-score region; injection 13 remains the fastest proven fully resolved method.

Use a slightly shallower gradient than injection 18 to improve the critical-pair margin while keeping the first peak comfortably retained. This tests another rapid maximum-score candidate without repeating a method; injection 13 remains the fastest proven option.

Lower temperature from injection 22 to increase the critical-pair margin while retaining a short gradient and adequately retained early peaks. This seeks a less marginal maximum-score alternative; injection 13 remains the fastest proven fully resolved method.

Shift the starting fraction up one step from injection 23 to test whether the shallower gradient improves the critical-pair margin without materially delaying the last peak. The maximum CRF is already secured, with injection 13 still the fastest proven fully resolved method.

Raise temperature one step from injection 24 to shorten late elution while testing whether its resolution margin preserves maximum CRF. Injection 13 remains the fastest proven maximum-score method, with all six peaks resolved by 2.58 minutes.
